slides.title: 16 Transitions. 1 Prompt. 0 Second Chances.
slides.subtitle: The status matrix is where vague prompts cost weeks

hero_stat.label: valid transitions across 6 states — every single one must be in the prompt or AI invents the wrong rule

analogy.title: Chess vs. checkers
analogy.text: Checkers: 1 piece, 4 moves. Easy to spec. Chess: 6 pieces, 64 squares, en passant. You can't 'figure it out as you go'. The status workflow is chess — every legal move must be on the board before you tell AI to play.

bullets: 6 states: Open · InProgress · InReview · Resolved · Closed · Reopened.
13 valid transitions + 2 explicitly illegal + 1 same-status-comment pattern = the famous 16.
Skip any one → AI invents a transition that breaks your audit trail.
Real cost of getting this wrong: 2-3 days of re-prompting after launch when QA finds it.
slides.closing_thread: Why is this AI's hardest territory? 4 reasons.
slides.narration: Sixteen transitions across six states. Open, InProgress, InReview, Resolved, Closed, Reopened. Every legal move must be in the prompt or AI invents the wrong rule. Real cost of skipping any one — two to three days of re-prompting after launch when QA finds it.

narration_script.speaker: Arjun
narration_script.text: Sixteen transitions. Across six states. This is the headline number for Module 5.

narration_script.speaker: Sara
narration_script.text: Six states — Open, InProgress, InReview, Resolved, Closed, Reopened. Thirteen valid transitions between them, two that must be explicitly illegal, one same-status-comment pattern. Sixteen total.

narration_script.speaker: Arjun
narration_script.text: Skip any one in the prompt — AI invents a transition. It might let you close an issue without resolving first. Or reopen one without a reason. Audit trail breaks. QA flags it. You re-prompt for two days.

slides.title: Why Workflows Are AI's Hardest Territory
slides.subtitle: 4 reasons — each one a trap if you don't plan for it

list.name: Domain-specific rules
list.desc: There is no 'standard' workflow. Yours is unique. AI has no training data for YOUR rules. If they're not in the prompt, AI invents plausible ones.

list.name: State explosion
list.desc: 6 states = 30 possible transitions (6 × 5). Most should be ILLEGAL. AI defaults to permissive unless you spell out the prohibitions.

list.name: Side-effects per transition
list.desc: Each transition might fire emails, update audit logs, lock fields. AI won't write side-effects unless explicitly told. Missed side-effects = silent bugs.

list.name: UI ↔ API parity
list.desc: The dropdown should show ONLY allowed next states. The API must enforce the same. AI often does one and not the other. UI ≠ enforcement.

slides.memory_hook: Domain rules · state explosion · side-effects · UI-API parity. Four traps. Each one needs explicit prompt language.
slides.closing_thread: How do we beat all four? With ONE structured prompt.

analogy.title: Air traffic control briefing
analogy.text: A pilot doesn't ask the tower 'what should I do?'. They get a flight plan: waypoints, altitudes, restricted zones, escalation rules. The workflow prompt is the flight plan — every legal move explicit, every illegal one named.

bullets: Section 1 — the state diagram (ASCII): Open → InProgress → InReview → (Resolved → Closed) ↺ Reopened
Section 2 — the transition matrix table: 16 rows, columns From / To / Allowed Roles / Required Fields / Side-effects.
Section 3 — illegal transitions: Open → Resolved (must go via InReview). InProgress → Resolved (same). State 400 + message.
Section 4 — comment rules: every status change requires a non-empty comment. Resolved requires resolution note. Reopened requires reason.
Section 5 — UI parity: status dropdown shows current + allowed next ONLY. Backend enforces the same matrix in middleware.

slides.subtitle: Same intent. Wildly different output.

Vague gets you a status field with assumed transitions, no illegal moves, no comment rules, basic dropdown. narration_script.speaker: Sara
narration_script.text: VAGUE — 'add status field with a few values'. AI guesses three to four values. Maybe Open, In Progress, Done. No matrix. No illegals. Permissive. Done is final and you can magically uncomplete. Auditor's nightmare.

narration_script.speaker: Arjun
narration_script.text: STRUCTURED — explicit six-state enum, named, ordered, with role assignments. Sixteen-row matrix with From, To, Roles, Required Fields, Side-effects. Illegal transitions named — Open arrow Resolved returns four hundred.

narration_script.speaker: Sara
narration_script.text: Mandatory comments. Resolution requires resolution note. Reopen requires reason. Dropdown filters. Backend re-validates. Belt and suspenders. AI does exactly what you specced — no drift.

slides.title: What Goes IN the Workflow Prompt
slides.subtitle: 5 explicit sections — none optional

list.name: State enum + diagram
list.desc: Name every state. Order them. Show an ASCII diagram of valid arrows. AI reads the diagram like spec text.

list.name: Transition matrix
list.desc: Table format. From, To, Allowed Roles, Required Fields, Side-effects. Every row a contract. No row, no transition.

list.name: Illegal transitions
list.desc: Name them. Set HTTP status (400). Set error message. AI must REJECT, not redirect or hide.

list.name: Comment & field rules
list.desc: What's mandatory at each transition. Resolution note for Resolved. Reason for Reopened. Audit log entry always.

list.name: UI-API parity contract
list.desc: Explicit: 'dropdown shows allowed-next; API re-validates'. Without this clause AI does ONE and skips the other.

slides.title: The Marker Pillar — Operationalised

slides.title: Day 5 — The Collaboration Layer
slides.subtitle: Comments + attachments — every Issue Tracker's social spine
bullets: Comments aren't just text — they're the AUDIT TRAIL of how an issue moved.
Every comment is tied to the status it was posted in. Some comments cause status changes. Both are first-class.
Attachments add another dimension: file size limits, MIME-type whitelists, virus scan hooks, signed URLs.
Get either wrong and you've got either a tampered audit trail (huge problem) or an XSS / RCE vector via file upload.

slides.title: The Comments + Status Prompt
slides.subtitle: Status dropdown · mandatory comment · resolution + reason rules

hero_stat.label: 1 component (CommentBox) · 12 endpoint behaviours · 4 mandatory field rules

bullets: Status dropdown rule: shows CURRENT status + ALLOWED next statuses only (per the matrix). NO 'no change' option.
Posting with current status: comment is saved; NO transition record. Audit log shows a comment event only.
Posting with new status: comment is saved; transition record written; side-effects fire (emails, notifications).
Resolved → required resolution note (separate field). Reopened → required reason (separate field). Both validated server-side.
Attachments on comment: up to 5 files per comment, ≤10 MB each, MIME whitelist (pdf, png, jpg, txt, docx). Server validates.
slides.memory_hook: Status + Comment = ONE form, TWO outcomes (transition or just-comment). Server enforces both paths.
slides.closing_thread: What the renderer generated — comment rules in code.

slides.title: File Upload Security — Safe vs Unsafe
slides.subtitle: AI defaults to UNSAFE unless you explicitly clamp

table.orch: ✅ Hard cap 10 MB per file, enforced before disk write
✅ UUID rename; original stored as metadata only
✅ Signed URL with expiry; non-guessable path; not in web root
✅ ClamAV hook OR S3 + Lambda scanner before serve

slides.memory_hook: Trust nothing from the client. Validate everything server-side. AI defaults are UNSAFE — clamp explicitly.
slides.closing_thread: Manual validation: post a comment with status change, attach a file, watch the audit log.
slides.narration: File upload security. Safe versus unsafe. AI defaults to unsafe unless you explicitly clamp. MIME validation — magic-byte check on server, not the Content-Type header. File size — hard cap before disk write. Filename — UUID rename. Storage — signed URL with expiry. Virus scan — ClamAV or S3 plus Lambda.

narration_script.speaker: Arjun
narration_script.text: File upload security. AI's default is UNSAFE. You explicitly clamp.

narration_script.speaker: Sara
narration_script.text: MIME validation — DON'T trust the Content-Type header. DO magic-byte check on the server with libmagic or file-type. File size — hard cap, ten megabytes per file, enforced BEFORE disk write.

narration_script.speaker: Arjun
narration_script.text: Filename storage — DON'T save original filename to disk. DO UUID rename, store original as metadata only. Storage location — DON'T put files in a predictable web-root path.

slides.title: The Bug AI Almost Always Gets Wrong: Closed → Reopen
slides.subtitle: First-pass behaviour vs what the FDD demands
bullets: FDD demands: Closed issues are LOCKED. No inline comments. Only a Reopen dialog with mandatory reason.
AI first pass typically: lets you comment on Closed issues normally. Lets you Reopen WITHOUT a reason.
Why? Closed → Reopen is one of the 16 transitions but it has a SPECIAL UI rule (dialog only) that vague prompts miss.
Symptoms QA finds: closed issues showing new comments, reopened issues with no reason in audit log.
slides.closing_thread: Here's the re-prompt that fixed it.
slides.narration: The bug AI almost always gets wrong. Closed arrow Reopen. FDD demands closed issues are locked — no inline comments, only a Reopen dialog with mandatory reason. AI first pass lets you comment on closed issues normally and reopen without a reason. Why? Closed-to-Reopen has a special UI rule that vague prompts miss.

narration_script.speaker: Sara
narration_script.text: The bug AI almost always gets wrong on first pass. Closed arrow Reopen.

narration_script.speaker: Arjun
narration_script.text: What the FDD demands — closed issues are LOCKED. No inline comments. Only a dedicated Reopen dialog. Mandatory reason in the dialog.

narration_script.speaker: Sara

narration_script.speaker: Arjun
narration_script.text: Why? Closed arrow Reopen is one of the sixteen transitions but it has a SPECIAL UI rule — dialog only — that vague prompts miss. Even good ones.

slides.title: The Surgical Re-Prompt That Fixed It
slides.subtitle: 3 sentences · references the exact files · names the exact fix

hero_stat.label: fixed 4 files · 1 component + 1 dialog + 1 service + 1 test — total time ~15 minutes

bullets: Bad re-prompt: 'fix the Closed issue thing' — vague, AI guesses, you waste a turn.
Good re-prompt (3 sentences):
→ "In CommentSection.tsx, when issue.status === 'Closed', do not render the inline comment form. Render a locked message + Reopen button instead."
→ "On Reopen button click, open ReopenDialog with a required 'reason' textarea (min 10 chars)."
→ "In issue.service.ts, transition to Reopened must reject if reason is missing or under 10 chars — return 400 with message."
Result: 4 files changed, 1 component + 1 dialog + 1 service + 1 unit test added. ~15 min total.
slides.memory_hook: Surgical re-prompt = name the file, name the function/component, name the fix-shape. 3 sentences max.
slides.closing_thread: And NOW — the part most learners skip: commit it.
slides.narration: The surgical re-prompt. Three sentences. References the exact files. Names the exact fix. In CommentSection.tsx, when issue status equals Closed, don't render the form. Render a locked message plus Reopen button. On Reopen click, open dialog with required reason textarea. In issue.service.ts, reject the transition if reason missing or under ten chars — return 400.

narration_script.speaker: Arjun
narration_script.text: The surgical re-prompt. Three sentences. Naming the EXACT files, EXACT changes.

narration_script.speaker: Sara
narration_script.text: Sentence one — in CommentSection-dot-tsx, when issue-dot-status equals Closed, don't render the inline comment form. Render a locked message plus Reopen button instead.

narration_script.speaker: Arjun
narration_script.text: Sentence two — on Reopen button click, open ReopenDialog with a required reason textarea, minimum ten characters.

narration_script.speaker: Sara
narration_script.text: Sentence three — in issue-dot-service-dot-ts, transition to Reopened must REJECT if reason is missing or under ten chars. Return four hundred with message.

narration_script.speaker: Arjun

slides.title: Commit Per Validated Component — The Habit That Saves You
slides.subtitle: The thing you should've done from Day 1 — fixing the gap now
slides.opening_hook: AI generates code at machine speed. Without Git, you can't roll back ANYTHING. Without commits, you have no history.
bullets: If you didn't git init on Day 1 — do it now: cd into project folder → git init → add a .gitignore → git add . → git commit -m 'initial scaffold'.
Create a GitHub repo (private). Add it as remote: git remote add origin <your-repo-url>. Push: git push -u origin main.
From here forward — commit per VALIDATED component. Not per AI generation. Validate first, commit second.
Example commit messages: 'feat(auth): JWT + bcrypt + route guards validated', 'fix(workflow): closed→reopen dialog reason required'.
End-of-day push: git push. Your GitHub now mirrors your local. This becomes your submission artifact in Module 6.
slides.memory_hook: Commit per validated component. Push end of day. GitHub IS your audit trail — pillar 1 of OGE, made tangible.
slides.closing_thread: Standard Git commands reference — next slide.

slides.title: 5 Things You DON'T Delegate

list.name: DB indexes

list.name: RLS / scoped queries
list.desc: Row-level security or service-layer scoping by user.tenantId. Re-verify every list endpoint never leaks across tenants. AI is permissive by default.

list.name: File upload sanitisation
list.desc: Magic-byte MIME check, UUID rename, signed URL, virus scan. Even with these specced, audit the implementation. Read the code. Don't trust the toast.

list.name: Audit log integrity
list.desc: Audit log entries must be APPEND-ONLY (no UPDATE / DELETE from any endpoint). Verify with Postgres role permissions on the table.

list.name: Workflow boundary tests
list.desc: Hit each illegal transition with curl. All return 400. ALL of them. This is your insurance policy when QA opens 30 bugs in Module 6.

slides.title: Spot the workflow prompt failures
slides.subtitle: Click each clause that breaks the 5-section workflow prompt rule
slides.text: Add a status workflow with states Open InProgress and Done. Users can change status by selecting it. Allow comments. The closed status should be final but maybe people can reopen.

flaws.explanation: Three states only — the FDD specifies six. Missing InReview, Resolved, Reopened. AI ships an incomplete state machine and your client's process is broken from day one.

flaws.phrase: Users can change status by selecting it
flaws.explanation: Who can change WHAT? No role allow-list. No matrix. AI ships a free-for-all where Reporters can close other people's issues. RBAC missing entirely.
Allowed how? Mandatory on status change? Resolution note required on close? Reopen reason? None specified. Audit trail will be flat, useless, and probably tampered with.
'Maybe' is not a spec. AI invents a permissive reopen with no reason field, no dialog, no guard. This is the EXACT bug we covered in Act 4. Repeats forever until prompts get explicit.
